name: CN I – Olfactory nerve
function: Special sensory nerve for smell; olfactory fila from the nasal roof pass through the cribriform plate to the olfactory bulb and tract.

details.label: Type
details.value: Special sensory (olfaction)

details.label: Exit foramen
details.value: Cribriform plate of ethmoid (foramina)

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Olfactory epithelium of superior nasal cavity (superior concha, septum)

details.label: Branches
details.value: ~20 olfactory fila -> olfactory bulb -> olfactory tract (no brainstem nucleus)

pearl: Anterior cranial fossa / cribriform fracture -> anosmia + CSF rhinorrhea. Anosmia also in Kallmann syndrome (with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism) and early Parkinson disease.

name: CN II – Optic nerve
function: Special sensory nerve for vision; retinal ganglion cell axons pass through the optic canal to the chiasm, optic tract and lateral geniculate nucleus.

details.label: Type
details.value: Special sensory (vision); CNS tract wrapped in meninges

details.label: Exit foramen
details.value: Optic canal (with ophthalmic artery)

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Retina -> optic chiasm -> optic tract -> LGN / pretectum (light reflex afferent)

details.label: Branches
details.value: None; nasal fibers decussate at chiasm

pearl: Optic neuritis (MS): painful monocular vision loss, RAPD (Marcus Gunn pupil), red desaturation. Papilledema with raised ICP because the nerve sheath carries CSF.

name: CN III – Oculomotor nerve
function: Motor to most extraocular muscles and levator palpebrae; carries preganglionic parasympathetics for pupillary constriction and accommodation.

details.label: Type
details.value: Somatic motor + parasympathetic (Edinger-Westphal)

details.label: Exit foramen
details.value: Superior orbital fissure (via lateral wall of cavernous sinus)

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Superior, inferior, medial rectus; inferior oblique; levator palpebrae; sphincter pupillae & ciliary muscle via ciliary ganglion

details.label: Branches
details.value: Superior division (SR, levator); inferior division (MR, IR, IO, parasympathetic root to ciliary ganglion)

pearl: Compressive palsy (PCom aneurysm, uncal herniation) hits superficial parasympathetic fibers first -> blown pupil. Diabetic/ischemic palsy spares the pupil: ptosis, eye 'down and out'.

name: CN IV – Trochlear nerve
function: Motor to the superior oblique, which depresses, intorts and abducts the eye; the only cranial nerve exiting the dorsal brainstem.

details.label: Type
details.value: Somatic motor

details.label: Exit foramen
details.value: Superior orbital fissure (outside annulus of Zinn), via cavernous sinus

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Superior oblique (contralateral nucleus; fibers decussate dorsally)

details.label: Branches
details.value: None; longest intracranial course, thinnest CN

pearl: Palsy -> vertical diplopia worst looking down and in (stairs, reading); patient tilts head AWAY from the lesion. Common after closed head trauma.

name: CN V – Trigeminal nerve
function: Chief sensory nerve of the face and motor nerve of mastication; three divisions arise from the trigeminal (Gasserian) ganglion in Meckel cave.

details.label: Type
details.value: Mixed: general sensory (V1-V3) + branchial motor (V3)

details.label: Exit foramen
details.value: V1 superior orbital fissure; V2 foramen rotundum; V3 foramen ovale

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Face, scalp to vertex, oral/nasal mucosa, teeth, dura; muscles of mastication, mylohyoid, ant. digastric, tensor tympani, tensor veli palatini

details.label: Branches
details.value: Ophthalmic (V1), maxillary (V2), mandibular (V3)

pearl: Trigeminal neuralgia: brief lancinating V2/V3 pain triggered by touch or chewing (vascular compression); first-line carbamazepine. Motor lesion -> jaw deviates toward the weak side.

name: CN VI – Abducens nerve
function: Motor to the lateral rectus, abducting the eye; runs a long course over the clivus and through the cavernous sinus beside the internal carotid.

details.label: Type
details.value: Somatic motor

details.label: Exit foramen
details.value: Superior orbital fissure (within annulus of Zinn) after Dorello canal and cavernous sinus

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Lateral rectus

details.label: Branches
details.value: None

pearl: Long intracranial course makes it the first nerve to fail with raised ICP (false localizing sign): horizontal diplopia, esotropia, cannot abduct. Also cavernous sinus thrombosis.

name: CN VII – Facial nerve
function: Motor to muscles of facial expression, taste from anterior 2/3 of tongue, and parasympathetics to lacrimal, submandibular and sublingual glands.

details.label: Type
details.value: Mixed: branchial motor, special sensory (taste), parasympathetic, small general sensory

details.label: Exit foramen
details.value: Internal acoustic meatus -> facial canal -> stylomastoid foramen

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Facial expression muscles, stapedius, posterior digastric, stylohyoid; taste ant. 2/3 tongue; lacrimal, nasal, submandibular, sublingual glands

details.label: Branches
details.value: Greater petrosal, nerve to stapedius, chorda tympani (intracanal); posterior auricular; temporal, zygomatic, buccal, marginal mandibular, cervical

pearl: Bell palsy (LMN) involves the forehead; UMN stroke spares it. Treat with prednisone +/- valacyclovir and eye protection. Ramsay Hunt = VZV with vesicles in the ear canal.

name: CN VIII – Vestibulocochlear nerve
function: Special sensory nerve for hearing (cochlear division) and balance (vestibular division), entering the brainstem at the cerebellopontine angle.

details.label: Type
details.value: Special sensory (hearing, equilibrium)

details.label: Exit foramen
details.value: Internal acoustic meatus (with CN VII and labyrinthine artery)

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Cochlea (spiral ganglion); utricle, saccule, semicircular canals (vestibular ganglion)

details.label: Branches
details.value: Cochlear nerve, vestibular nerve (superior and inferior)

pearl: Vestibular schwannoma at the cerebellopontine angle: unilateral sensorineural loss, tinnitus, imbalance; bilateral = NF2. Weber lateralizes to the better ear, Rinne AC > BC.

name: CN IX – Glossopharyngeal nerve
function: Mixed nerve to the pharynx and posterior tongue: taste and sensation of posterior 1/3 tongue, carotid body/sinus afferents, motor to stylopharyngeus, parasympathetics to parotid.

details.label: Type
details.value: Mixed: sensory, taste, branchial motor, parasympathetic

details.label: Exit foramen
details.value: Jugular foramen (with X, XI)

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Stylopharyngeus; posterior 1/3 tongue, oropharynx, tonsil, middle ear; carotid sinus/body; parotid via otic ganglion

details.label: Branches
details.value: Tympanic (Jacobson), carotid sinus (Hering), pharyngeal, stylopharyngeal, tonsillar, lingual

pearl: Lesion -> loss of gag reflex afferent limb and posterior tongue taste. Glossopharyngeal neuralgia: swallowing-triggered throat/ear pain that can cause bradycardia and syncope.

name: CN X – Vagus nerve
function: Motor to pharynx, palate and larynx, sensory from larynx/pharynx, and parasympathetic supply to thoracic and abdominal viscera as far as the splenic flexure.

details.label: Type
details.value: Mixed: branchial motor, parasympathetic, visceral and general sensory, taste (epiglottis)

details.label: Exit foramen
details.value: Jugular foramen; descends in carotid sheath between ICA/CCA and IJV

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Pharyngeal constrictors, palate (except tensor veli palatini), all laryngeal muscles; heart, lungs, gut; skin of EAM

details.label: Branches
details.value: Auricular (Arnold), pharyngeal, superior laryngeal, recurrent laryngeal, cardiac, pulmonary, esophageal

pearl: Palsy -> uvula deviates AWAY from the lesion, dysphagia, hoarseness, lost gag efferent limb. Vasovagal syncope and carotid sinus reflex run through it.

name: CN XI – Accessory nerve
function: Motor nerve to the sternocleidomastoid and trapezius; its spinal root ascends through the foramen magnum and exits via the jugular foramen.

details.label: Type
details.value: Branchial (somatic) motor

details.label: Exit foramen
details.value: Jugular foramen (spinal root C1-C5 enters skull via foramen magnum)

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Sternocleidomastoid, trapezius (cranial root fibers join vagus to pharynx/larynx)

details.label: Branches
details.value: Spinal root -> branches to SCM, then crosses posterior triangle superficially (SCM posterior border to anterior border of trapezius) -> trapezius; cranial root joins CN X

pearl: Injured in posterior triangle lymph node biopsy or neck dissection -> shoulder droop, cannot shrug, scapular winging on abduction, weak head turn to the opposite side.

name: CN XII – Hypoglossal nerve
function: Motor nerve of the tongue, supplying all intrinsic and extrinsic tongue muscles except palatoglossus; carries C1 fibers to geniohyoid and thyrohyoid.

details.label: Type
details.value: Somatic motor

details.label: Exit foramen
details.value: Hypoglossal canal; descends between ICA and IJV, hooks around occipital artery, passes above hyoid on hyoglossus

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Genioglossus, hyoglossus, styloglossus, intrinsic tongue muscles (palatoglossus = X)

details.label: Branches
details.value: Lingual branches; superior root of ansa cervicalis (C1 fibers), nerve to thyrohyoid and geniohyoid (C1)

pearl: LMN lesion -> tongue deviates TOWARD the lesion with atrophy and fasciculations. At risk in carotid endarterectomy and submandibular surgery.

name: Ophthalmic division (V1)
function: Purely sensory division of the trigeminal supplying the forehead, scalp to vertex, upper eyelid, cornea, nose and frontal/ethmoid sinuses; afferent limb of the corneal reflex.

details.label: Type
details.value: General sensory

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Lateral wall of cavernous sinus -> superior orbital fissure

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Forehead, upper eyelid, cornea/conjunctiva, dorsum and tip of nose, frontal & ethmoid sinuses, tentorium

details.label: Branches
details.value: Frontal, lacrimal, nasociliary; recurrent tentorial (meningeal)

pearl: Herpes zoster ophthalmicus: vesicles in V1 dermatome; Hutchinson sign (nasal tip lesion via nasociliary) predicts ocular involvement. Cavernous sinus lesions involve V1 (and V2) but spare V3.

name: Supraorbital nerve
function: Terminal branch of the frontal nerve (V1) that exits the supraorbital foramen to supply the forehead, anterior scalp to the vertex, upper eyelid and frontal sinus mucosa.

details.label: Type
details.value: General sensory

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Supraorbital foramen or notch, with supraorbital artery

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Forehead skin, scalp to vertex, upper eyelid, conjunctiva, frontal sinus

details.label: Branches
details.value: Medial and lateral branches

pearl: Supraorbital pressure is a standard painful stimulus in GCS/coma assessment. Supraorbital + supratrochlear block anesthetizes the forehead for laceration repair.

name: Nasociliary nerve
function: V1 branch crossing the orbit medially; supplies the cornea via long ciliary nerves, the ethmoid air cells and nasal cavity, and the nasal tip via the external nasal branch.

details.label: Type
details.value: General sensory (carries sympathetics to dilator pupillae via long ciliary)

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Superior orbital fissure within the annulus of Zinn, crosses above the optic nerve

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Cornea, iris, ciliary body; ethmoid & sphenoid sinuses, nasal septum; skin of nose dorsum and tip; medial eyelids

details.label: Branches
details.value: Sensory root to ciliary ganglion, long ciliary, posterior & anterior ethmoidal (-> external nasal), infratrochlear

pearl: Corneal reflex afferent (long ciliary). Hutchinson sign: nasal-tip zoster predicts eye involvement. FESS: anterior ethmoidal artery injury -> orbital hematoma; CSF leak if the thin lateral lamella beside it is breached.

name: Frontal nerve
function: Largest branch of V1; runs forward on the levator palpebrae beneath the orbital roof and divides into the supraorbital and supratrochlear nerves.

details.label: Type
details.value: General sensory

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Superior orbital fissure above the annulus of Zinn, along orbital roof

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Forehead, scalp, upper eyelid, medial canthus (via supratrochlear), frontal sinus

details.label: Branches
details.value: Supraorbital (lateral, larger), supratrochlear (medial)

pearl: Lies just beneath the orbital roof, so orbital roof fractures or frontal sinus surgery can cause forehead numbness; supratrochlear block numbs the medial forehead and glabella.

name: Lacrimal nerve
function: Smallest V1 branch running along the upper border of the lateral rectus to the lacrimal gland, conjunctiva and lateral upper eyelid; relays parasympathetic fibers from the zygomatic nerve.

details.label: Type
details.value: General sensory (+ carries postganglionic parasympathetics to lacrimal gland)

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Superior orbital fissure (lateral, outside annulus), along lateral orbital wall

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Lacrimal gland, lateral conjunctiva, lateral upper eyelid skin

details.label: Branches
details.value: Communicating branch with zygomaticotemporal nerve

pearl: Secretomotor fibers reach the gland via VII -> greater petrosal -> pterygopalatine ganglion -> zygomatic -> lacrimal; a facial nerve lesion proximal to the geniculate ganglion causes dry eye.

name: Maxillary division (V2)
function: Purely sensory division passing through the foramen rotundum into the pterygopalatine fossa; supplies the midface, maxillary teeth, palate, nasal cavity and maxillary sinus.

details.label: Type
details.value: General sensory

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Foramen rotundum -> pterygopalatine fossa -> inferior orbital fissure (as infraorbital nerve)

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Lower eyelid, cheek, side of nose, upper lip, maxillary teeth and gingiva, hard/soft palate, nasal cavity, nasopharynx, maxillary sinus

details.label: Branches
details.value: Meningeal, zygomatic, pterygopalatine (nasopalatine, greater/lesser palatine, pharyngeal), posterior superior alveolar, infraorbital

pearl: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma and perineural spread of skin cancer track along V2 through foramen rotundum; maxillary sinus tumors present with cheek numbness. Zygomaticomaxillary fractures injure it.

name: Infraorbital nerve
function: Terminal continuation of V2 through the infraorbital groove, canal and foramen to the lower eyelid, side of nose, upper lip and anterior maxillary teeth.

details.label: Type
details.value: General sensory

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Inferior orbital fissure -> infraorbital groove/canal -> infraorbital foramen (~1 cm below orbital rim)

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Lower eyelid, ala and side of nose, upper lip, cheek; incisors to premolars via anterior and middle superior alveolar nerves

details.label: Branches
details.value: Anterior & middle superior alveolar, inferior palpebral, nasal, superior labial

pearl: Orbital floor blowout fracture: infraorbital numbness (cheek, upper lip, teeth) plus diplopia on upgaze from inferior rectus entrapment. Infraorbital block numbs the upper lip.

name: Zygomatic nerve (V2)
function: V2 branch entering the orbit through the inferior orbital fissure to supply skin over the cheek and temple; carries parasympathetic fibers onward to the lacrimal nerve.

details.label: Type
details.value: General sensory (+ postganglionic parasympathetic carrier)

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Pterygopalatine fossa -> inferior orbital fissure -> lateral orbital wall -> zygomatic bone foramina

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Skin of prominence of cheek (zygomaticofacial), anterior temple (zygomaticotemporal)

details.label: Branches
details.value: Zygomaticofacial, zygomaticotemporal, communicating branch to lacrimal nerve

pearl: Secretomotor fibers from the pterygopalatine ganglion hitch a ride on the zygomaticotemporal branch to reach the lacrimal gland; zygomatic fractures cause cheek numbness.

name: Mandibular division (V3)
function: Only trigeminal division with motor fibers; exits through the foramen ovale into the infratemporal fossa to supply mastication muscles and sensation to the lower face, tongue and mandibular teeth.

details.label: Type
details.value: Mixed: general sensory + branchial motor

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Foramen ovale -> infratemporal fossa (divides into anterior and posterior trunks)

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Masseter, temporalis, pterygoids, mylohyoid, ant. digastric, tensor tympani, tensor veli palatini; chin, lower lip, cheek, temple, auricle, ant. 2/3 tongue, mandibular teeth

details.label: Branches
details.value: Meningeal, n. to medial pterygoid, masseteric, deep temporal, n. to lateral pterygoid, buccal, auriculotemporal, lingual, inferior alveolar (-> n. to mylohyoid)

pearl: Motor lesion -> jaw deviates toward the weak side on opening, weak bite. Nasopharyngeal carcinoma invades via foramen ovale; V3 is spared in cavernous sinus syndromes.

name: Auriculotemporal nerve
function: V3 branch whose roots encircle the middle meningeal artery; passes behind the TMJ and ascends with the superficial temporal artery to supply the auricle, EAM, TMJ and temple; relays parasympathetics to the parotid.

details.label: Type
details.value: General sensory + postganglionic parasympathetic (from otic ganglion)

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Posterior trunk of V3 -> around middle meningeal artery -> deep to parotid behind TMJ -> ascends anterior to tragus

details.label: Supplies
details.value: TMJ, skin of auricle, EAM, outer tympanic membrane, temple; parotid secretomotor

details.label: Branches
details.value: Anterior auricular, auricular branches to EAM and tympanic membrane, articular (TMJ), parotid, superficial temporal, communicating branches to CN VII

pearl: Frey syndrome after parotidectomy: regenerating parotid parasympathetic fibers reinnervate facial sweat glands -> gustatory sweating/flushing of the cheek. Also carries TMJ and parotid pain referred to the ear.

name: Lingual nerve
function: V3 branch giving general sensation to the anterior 2/3 of the tongue and floor of mouth; joined by the chorda tympani, so it also carries taste and parasympathetic fibers.

details.label: Type
details.value: General sensory (+ taste and preganglionic parasympathetic via chorda tympani)

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Infratemporal fossa -> medial to ramus -> lateral to hyoglossus -> loops under submandibular (Wharton) duct

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Anterior 2/3 tongue (general sensation), floor of mouth, lingual gingiva

details.label: Branches
details.value: Branches to submandibular ganglion, sublingual nerve, lingual branches

pearl: At risk in third molar extraction and submandibular gland excision (passes beneath Wharton duct) -> loss of sensation and taste on the anterior tongue.

name: Inferior alveolar nerve
function: Largest V3 branch entering the mandibular foramen to run in the mandibular canal, supplying all mandibular teeth and ending as the mental and incisive nerves.

details.label: Type
details.value: General sensory (+ motor nerve to mylohyoid before entering canal)

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Mandibular foramen (medial ramus, at lingula) -> mandibular canal -> mental foramen

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Mandibular teeth and gingiva, lower lip, chin; mylohyoid and anterior digastric via its branch

details.label: Branches
details.value: Nerve to mylohyoid, inferior dental plexus, mental nerve, incisive nerve

pearl: Dental IAN block at the lingula numbs lower teeth, lip and chin. Mandibular body/angle fractures and bisphosphonate osteonecrosis cause lip/chin numbness.

name: Mental nerve
function: Terminal sensory branch of the inferior alveolar nerve exiting the mental foramen to supply the chin, lower lip skin and mucosa, and labial gingiva.

details.label: Type
details.value: General sensory

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Mental foramen (below 2nd premolar, in line with supraorbital and infraorbital foramina)

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Skin of chin, lower lip skin and mucosa, labial gingiva of incisors/premolars

details.label: Branches
details.value: Mental, inferior labial, gingival branches

pearl: Numb chin syndrome: isolated mental nerve neuropathy from mandibular metastasis (breast, lung, lymphoma) - a red flag for occult malignancy.

name: Buccal nerve (V3, sensory)
function: Sensory branch of the anterior trunk of V3 that emerges between the heads of the lateral pterygoid and runs onto the buccinator to supply the cheek skin and mucosa and molar gingiva.

details.label: Type
details.value: General sensory

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Between heads of lateral pterygoid -> deep to temporalis tendon -> pierces buccinator (does not supply it)

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Skin and mucosa of cheek, buccal gingiva of mandibular molars

details.label: Branches
details.value: Cutaneous and mucosal branches

pearl: Not the same as the buccal branch of CN VII (motor to buccinator). Long buccal block supplements IAN block for lower molar extraction.

name: Nerve to mylohyoid
function: Motor branch leaving the inferior alveolar nerve just before the mandibular foramen; runs in the mylohyoid groove to supply the mylohyoid and anterior belly of digastric.

details.label: Type
details.value: Branchial motor (small sensory contribution to chin)

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Mylohyoid groove on medial mandible -> superficial surface of mylohyoid

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Mylohyoid, anterior belly of digastric

details.label: Branches
details.value: Muscular branches

pearl: 'Two bellies, two nerves': anterior digastric = V3 (nerve to mylohyoid), posterior digastric = CN VII. It can supply the chin and cause IAN-block failure.

name: Temporal branch of facial nerve
function: Uppermost terminal branch of CN VII; leaves the parotid and crosses the zygomatic arch to supply frontalis, orbicularis oculi (upper), corrugator and auricular muscles.

details.label: Type
details.value: Branchial motor

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Exits parotid superiorly, crosses zygomatic arch midway between tragus and lateral canthus (Pitanguy line) within the temporoparietal fascia

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Frontalis, orbicularis oculi (upper part), corrugator supercilii, auricularis anterior/superior

details.label: Branches
details.value: Frontal (temporal) rami

pearl: Runs superficially over the zygomatic arch, so it is at risk in facelifts and temporal incisions; injury -> brow ptosis and inability to wrinkle the forehead.

name: Zygomatic branch of facial nerve
function: CN VII terminal branch crossing the zygomatic bone to the orbicularis oculi, responsible for forceful eye closure and the blink/corneal reflex efferent limb.

details.label: Type
details.value: Branchial motor

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Exits parotid anterosuperiorly across zygomatic bone toward lateral orbit

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Orbicularis oculi (lower and lateral), parts of zygomaticus and nasalis

details.label: Branches
details.value: Communicates with buccal branch

pearl: Injury -> lagophthalmos (incomplete eye closure) and exposure keratitis; this is why facial palsy patients need lubricant drops and eye taping at night.

name: Buccal branch of facial nerve
function: Motor branches of CN VII running with the parotid duct across the masseter to buccinator, orbicularis oris and the lip elevators; drives smiling, lip closure and cheek tone.

details.label: Type
details.value: Branchial motor

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Exits anterior parotid border, superficial to masseter, above and below the parotid (Stensen) duct

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Buccinator, orbicularis oris, zygomaticus major/minor, levator labii superioris, levator anguli oris, nasalis, risorius

details.label: Branches
details.value: Superior (deep) and inferior buccal rami

pearl: Injury -> food pools in the buccal vestibule, cannot puff cheeks or whistle, flattened nasolabial fold. Lacerations of the cheek that cut the duct usually cut this nerve too.

name: Marginal mandibular branch of facial nerve
function: CN VII branch running along the lower border of the mandible, often dipping below it in the submandibular triangle, to supply the lower lip depressors and mentalis.

details.label: Type
details.value: Branchial motor

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Exits lower parotid, deep to platysma, superficial to facial artery and vein; may lie 1-2 cm below the mandibular border

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Depressor anguli oris, depressor labii inferioris, mentalis, risorius (part)

details.label: Branches
details.value: Rami to lower lip muscles

pearl: At risk in submandibular gland excision/neck dissection: incise 2+ cm below the mandible, ligate facial vessels low. Injury -> asymmetric smile: affected lower lip cannot depress/evert and sits higher than normal side.

name: Cervical branch of facial nerve
function: Lowest terminal branch of CN VII, descending from the parotid into the neck deep to platysma, which it supplies.

details.label: Type
details.value: Branchial motor

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Exits inferior parotid pole, runs forward and down deep to platysma

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Platysma

details.label: Branches
details.value: Communicates with transverse cervical nerve (C2-C3)

pearl: Injury in neck lift or parotid surgery -> pseudoparalysis of the lower lip (platysma aids lip depression), mimicking marginal mandibular injury but with intact mentalis.

name: Chorda tympani
function: Branch of CN VII carrying taste from the anterior 2/3 of the tongue and preganglionic parasympathetics to the submandibular ganglion; crosses the middle ear and joins the lingual nerve.

details.label: Type
details.value: Special sensory (taste) + preganglionic parasympathetic

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Leaves facial canal above stylomastoid foramen -> crosses medial surface of tympanic membrane between malleus handle and long process of incus -> petrotympanic fissure -> joins lingual nerve in infratemporal fossa

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Taste buds of anterior 2/3 tongue; submandibular and sublingual glands (via submandibular ganglion)

details.label: Branches
details.value: Joins lingual nerve; taste cell bodies in geniculate ganglion

pearl: Bell palsy (lesion proximal to its origin) or direct injury in middle ear surgery (e.g., stapedectomy) -> ipsilateral loss of anterior 2/3 tongue taste and reduced salivation; visible through the TM.

name: Greater petrosal nerve
function: First branch of CN VII, from the geniculate ganglion; carries preganglionic parasympathetics through the pterygoid canal to the pterygopalatine ganglion for lacrimal, nasal and palatine glands.

details.label: Type
details.value: Preganglionic parasympathetic + taste from palate

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Geniculate ganglion -> hiatus of facial canal -> foramen lacerum -> joins deep petrosal (sympathetic) as nerve of pterygoid canal (Vidian) -> pterygopalatine ganglion

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Lacrimal gland, nasal, palatine and pharyngeal mucous glands; taste from soft palate

details.label: Branches
details.value: Nerve of the pterygoid canal (with deep petrosal nerve)

pearl: Facial nerve lesion at or proximal to the geniculate ganglion -> dry eye (reduced tearing), which localizes the lesion; aberrant regeneration -> crocodile tears when eating.

name: Nerve to stapedius
function: Tiny motor branch arising from CN VII in the descending facial canal to the stapedius, which damps stapes vibration and protects the cochlea from loud sound.

details.label: Type
details.value: Branchial motor

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Arises in vertical (mastoid) segment of facial canal, enters pyramidal eminence of middle ear

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Stapedius muscle

details.label: Branches
details.value: None

pearl: Facial lesion proximal to this branch -> hyperacusis (sounds painfully loud); an absent acoustic (stapedial) reflex on tympanometry helps localize the lesion.

name: Posterior auricular nerve
function: First extracranial branch of CN VII, arising just below the stylomastoid foramen and running up behind the ear to the occipitalis and posterior auricular muscles.

details.label: Type
details.value: Branchial motor (+ small sensory to auricle)

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Just below stylomastoid foramen, ascends between mastoid and auricle with posterior auricular artery

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Occipitalis, auricularis posterior, intrinsic auricular muscles

details.label: Branches
details.value: Auricular and occipital branches

pearl: Given off before the trunk enters the parotid, so spared by intraparotid tumors. In parotidectomy the facial trunk is found just above its origin using the tragal pointer, tympanomastoid suture and posterior belly of digastric as landmarks.

name: Tympanic nerve (Jacobson) / lesser petrosal nerve
function: CN IX branch forming the tympanic plexus on the middle ear promontory, then continuing as the lesser petrosal nerve carrying preganglionic parasympathetics to the otic ganglion for the parotid.

details.label: Type
details.value: Preganglionic parasympathetic + general sensory (middle ear)

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Inferior ganglion of IX -> tympanic canaliculus -> tympanic plexus -> lesser petrosal -> foramen ovale -> otic ganglion -> auriculotemporal -> parotid

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Mucosa of middle ear, mastoid air cells, Eustachian tube (sensory); parotid gland (secretomotor)

details.label: Branches
details.value: Tympanic plexus, lesser petrosal nerve, caroticotympanic communications

pearl: Explains referred otalgia from tonsillitis, post-tonsillectomy and oropharyngeal cancer (CN IX). Glomus tympanicum paragangliomas arise from Jacobson nerve -> pulsatile tinnitus.

name: Carotid sinus nerve (Hering)
function: Visceral afferent branch of CN IX descending to the carotid bifurcation; carries baroreceptor input from the carotid sinus and chemoreceptor input from the carotid body to the solitary nucleus.

details.label: Type
details.value: Visceral sensory (afferent)

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: From IX just below jugular foramen, descends on internal carotid artery to bifurcation

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Carotid sinus baroreceptors (stretch), carotid body chemoreceptors (O2, CO2, pH)

details.label: Branches
details.value: Joins with vagal and sympathetic fibers at the carotid sinus

pearl: Afferent limb of the baroreflex: carotid sinus massage or tight collars -> bradycardia and syncope (carotid sinus hypersensitivity); efferent limb runs via the vagus.

name: Pharyngeal branch of vagus / pharyngeal plexus
function: Main motor nerve of the pharynx and soft palate; joins IX and sympathetic fibers on the middle constrictor to form the pharyngeal plexus.

details.label: Type
details.value: Branchial motor (vagus; fibers partly from cranial root of XI)

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: From inferior (nodose) ganglion, passes between ICA and ECA to the middle constrictor

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Superior, middle, inferior constrictors; levator veli palatini, palatoglossus, palatopharyngeus, salpingopharyngeus, musculus uvulae

details.label: Branches
details.value: Pharyngeal plexus (motor X, sensory IX, sympathetic from superior cervical ganglion)

pearl: Vagal lesion -> uvula deviates away from the lesion, nasal regurgitation, dysphagia. Palatoglossus is the only tongue muscle not supplied by XII; tensor veli palatini is V3.

name: Superior laryngeal nerve
function: Vagal branch descending medial to the internal carotid artery that divides at the greater horn of the hyoid into the internal (sensory) and external (motor) laryngeal nerves.

details.label: Type
details.value: Mixed (sensory internal branch, motor external branch)

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: From inferior (nodose) vagal ganglion, descends medial to ICA, divides at level of greater horn of hyoid

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Supraglottic larynx sensation (internal); cricothyroid and part of inferior constrictor (external)

details.label: Branches
details.value: Internal laryngeal nerve (pierces thyrohyoid membrane), external laryngeal nerve (runs with superior thyroid artery)

pearl: External branch tracks the superior thyroid artery: ligate the artery close to the upper thyroid pole, not high, to spare it (injury -> loss of high pitch). Internal branch is the cough-reflex afferent, blocked at the thyrohyoid membrane for awake intubation.

name: Internal laryngeal nerve
function: Sensory branch of the superior laryngeal nerve that pierces the thyrohyoid membrane to supply laryngeal mucosa above the vocal folds, the epiglottis and the piriform recess.

details.label: Type
details.value: General and visceral sensory (+ taste from epiglottis, parasympathetic to glands)

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Pierces thyrohyoid membrane with superior laryngeal artery (branch of superior thyroid artery)

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Mucosa of supraglottic larynx (down to the vocal folds), vallecula, epiglottis, piriform recess

details.label: Branches
details.value: Superior and inferior branches; communicates with recurrent laryngeal (Galen anastomosis)

pearl: Afferent limb of the laryngeal cough reflex; injury (e.g., removing a fish bone from the piriform recess) -> loss of supraglottic sensation and aspiration. Blocked for awake intubation.

name: External laryngeal nerve
function: Motor branch of the superior laryngeal nerve that descends with the superior thyroid artery to the cricothyroid, the muscle that tenses the vocal folds and raises pitch.

details.label: Type
details.value: Branchial motor

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Descends on inferior constrictor alongside superior thyroid artery to upper pole of thyroid

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Cricothyroid; part of inferior pharyngeal constrictor

details.label: Branches
details.value: Muscular branches

pearl: Injured when ligating the superior thyroid artery in thyroidectomy -> cannot raise pitch, voice fatigue, monotone voice (singer's complaint) with normal-looking cords.

name: Recurrent laryngeal nerve
function: Vagal branch looping under the right subclavian artery or left aortic arch, ascending in the tracheoesophageal groove to supply all intrinsic laryngeal muscles except cricothyroid and infraglottic sensation.

details.label: Type
details.value: Mixed: branchial motor + sensory below vocal folds

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Right: loops under subclavian artery; left: under aortic arch (ligamentum arteriosum). Ascends in tracheoesophageal groove near inferior thyroid artery, enters larynx behind cricothyroid joint

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Posterior and lateral cricoarytenoids, thyroarytenoid, vocalis, arytenoids; mucosa below vocal folds; esophagus/trachea branches

details.label: Branches
details.value: Inferior laryngeal nerve (terminal), tracheal, esophageal, cardiac branches

pearl: Unilateral injury (thyroidectomy, apical lung or mediastinal tumor, aortic aneurysm) -> hoarseness. Bilateral injury -> stridor and airway obstruction from loss of posterior cricoarytenoid abduction.

name: Auricular branch of vagus (Arnold)
function: Sensory vagal branch from the superior ganglion that passes through the mastoid canaliculus and tympanomastoid fissure to the posterior ear canal, concha and outer tympanic membrane.

details.label: Type
details.value: General sensory

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Superior (jugular) ganglion -> mastoid canaliculus -> tympanomastoid fissure

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Skin of posterior/inferior external acoustic meatus, concha, outer tympanic membrane

details.label: Branches
details.value: Communicates with CN IX and VII (posterior auricular)

pearl: Arnold reflex: ear canal stimulation (cerumen removal, suction) triggers cough or syncope. Referred otalgia from laryngeal/hypopharyngeal cancer travels via the vagus.

name: Ciliary ganglion
function: Parasympathetic ganglion behind the eye where CN III fibers synapse; postganglionic short ciliary nerves constrict the pupil and contract the ciliary muscle for accommodation.

details.label: Type
details.value: Parasympathetic ganglion (CN III relay)

details.label: Location
details.value: Posterior orbit, lateral to optic nerve, medial to lateral rectus

details.label: Synapse
details.value: Preganglionic from Edinger-Westphal nucleus via inferior division of III (branch to inferior oblique)

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Sphincter pupillae, ciliary muscle via short ciliary nerves

details.label: Passes through unrelayed
details.value: Sympathetic fibers (dilator pupillae), sensory fibers from nasociliary nerve

pearl: Adie tonic pupil: viral damage to the ganglion/postganglionic fibers -> dilated pupil with poor light but slow tonic near response; constricts to dilute pilocarpine (denervation supersensitivity).

name: Pterygopalatine ganglion
function: Largest parasympathetic ganglion, suspended from V2 in the pterygopalatine fossa; relays facial nerve fibers to the lacrimal gland and the mucous glands of the nose, palate and nasopharynx.

details.label: Type
details.value: Parasympathetic ganglion (CN VII relay)

details.label: Location
details.value: Pterygopalatine fossa, below maxillary nerve, in front of pterygoid canal

details.label: Synapse
details.value: Preganglionic from superior salivatory nucleus via greater petrosal nerve / nerve of pterygoid canal

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Lacrimal gland (via zygomatic -> lacrimal nerve); nasal, palatine, pharyngeal glands (via V2 branches)

details.label: Passes through unrelayed
details.value: Sympathetic fibers (deep petrosal), sensory V2 fibers

pearl: Facial nerve lesion proximal to the geniculate ganglion cuts greater petrosal fibers -> dry eye; aberrant regeneration -> crocodile tears. Sphenopalatine ganglion block treats cluster and post-dural-puncture headache; juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma spreads through the pterygopalatine fossa.

name: Otic ganglion
function: Parasympathetic ganglion just below the foramen ovale, medial to V3, where lesser petrosal (CN IX) fibers synapse; postganglionic fibers reach the parotid via the auriculotemporal nerve.

details.label: Type
details.value: Parasympathetic ganglion (CN IX relay)

details.label: Location
details.value: Infratemporal fossa, immediately below foramen ovale, medial to mandibular nerve

details.label: Synapse
details.value: Preganglionic from inferior salivatory nucleus via tympanic nerve -> lesser petrosal nerve

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Parotid gland (secretomotor) via auriculotemporal nerve

details.label: Passes through unrelayed
details.value: Sympathetic fibers from middle meningeal plexus; motor fibers to tensor tympani/veli palatini

pearl: Parotid secretomotor supply is CN IX, not VII: IX -> tympanic -> lesser petrosal -> otic -> auriculotemporal. After parotidectomy, aberrant regeneration of these fibers into sweat glands causes Frey syndrome (gustatory sweating and flushing over the cheek).

name: Submandibular ganglion
function: Parasympathetic ganglion hanging from the lingual nerve on the hyoglossus; chorda tympani (CN VII) fibers synapse here to drive the submandibular and sublingual salivary glands.

details.label: Type
details.value: Parasympathetic ganglion (CN VII relay)

details.label: Location
details.value: On hyoglossus, suspended from lingual nerve above the deep part of the submandibular gland

details.label: Synapse
details.value: Preganglionic from superior salivatory nucleus via chorda tympani -> lingual nerve

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Submandibular and sublingual glands, anterior lingual glands

details.label: Passes through unrelayed
details.value: Sympathetic fibers from the facial artery plexus

pearl: Facial nerve or chorda tympani lesion -> reduced salivation on that side. The ganglion and lingual nerve are at risk in submandibular gland excision for sialolithiasis (most stones are in Wharton duct).

name: Cervical plexus (C1–C4)
function: Network formed by ventral rami of C1–C4 deep to SCM on levator scapulae and middle scalene; gives cutaneous branches to neck skin and motor branches to strap muscles and the diaphragm.

details.label: Type
details.value: Mixed (sensory cutaneous branches + motor branches)

details.label: Route
details.value: Ventral rami C1–C4 form loops anterior to transverse processes, deep to prevertebral fascia, IJV and SCM

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Skin of neck, posterolateral scalp, auricle, shoulder; infrahyoid muscles; diaphragm; prevertebral muscles

details.label: Cutaneous branches
details.value: Lesser occipital, great auricular, transverse cervical, supraclavicular (emerge at nerve point)

details.label: Motor branches
details.value: Ansa cervicalis, phrenic nerve, C1 fibers via CN XII, branches to prevertebral and scalene muscles

pearl: Superficial cervical plexus block at the nerve point anesthetizes neck skin for carotid endarterectomy; a deep block risks phrenic nerve palsy and intravascular/intrathecal injection.

name: Lesser occipital nerve (C2)
function: Cutaneous branch of C2 that ascends along the posterior border of SCM to supply the scalp behind and above the auricle.

details.label: Type
details.value: Sensory

details.label: Route
details.value: Emerges at nerve point, hooks around the spinal accessory nerve, ascends posterior border of SCM to the scalp

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Skin of lateral occipital scalp behind the ear and upper medial (cranial) surface of the auricle

details.label: Root
details.value: Ventral ramus C2 (sometimes C3)

pearl: Occipital neuralgia can involve the lesser or greater occipital nerve; a block along the posterior SCM border/superior nuchal line relieves lancinating posterior scalp pain.

name: Great auricular nerve (C2–C3)
function: Largest ascending branch of the cervical plexus; crosses SCM obliquely with the external jugular vein to supply skin over the parotid, mastoid, and lower auricle (lobule).

details.label: Type
details.value: Sensory

details.label: Route
details.value: Winds around posterior border of SCM at the nerve point, ascends on SCM parallel and posterior to the EJV toward the parotid

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Skin over parotid gland and angle of mandible, mastoid, both surfaces of the lower auricle and lobule

details.label: Roots
details.value: C2–C3

pearl: Most commonly injured nerve in parotidectomy and facelift (rhytidectomy): numb ear lobule. Lobule = C2–C3; the concha is CN VII/X and the tragus/anterior ear is auriculotemporal (V3).

name: Transverse cervical nerve (C2–C3)
function: Runs horizontally forward across SCM deep to platysma and the EJV to supply skin of the anterior triangle from mandible to sternum.

details.label: Type
details.value: Sensory

details.label: Route
details.value: Emerges at nerve point, crosses SCM horizontally deep to platysma, divides into ascending and descending branches

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Skin of the anterior neck (anterior triangle) from the lower border of the mandible to the sternum

details.label: Roots
details.value: C2–C3

details.label: Communication
details.value: Forms a plexus with the cervical branch of the facial nerve (CN VII) deep to platysma

pearl: Routinely cut in thyroidectomy and neck dissection incisions, causing anterior neck numbness; its link with the cervical branch of CN VII explains mixed sensory/platysma findings.

name: Supraclavicular nerves (C3–C4)
function: Descend from the nerve point as medial, intermediate, and lateral branches over the clavicle to supply skin of the lower neck, shoulder cap, and upper chest to the 2nd rib.

details.label: Type
details.value: Sensory

details.label: Route
details.value: Common trunk emerges under SCM, descends in posterior triangle, pierces deep fascia above the clavicle, branches cross it

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Skin over clavicle, sternoclavicular joint, shoulder (over deltoid/trapezius), upper pectoral region to 2nd rib

details.label: Branches
details.value: Medial, intermediate, lateral supraclavicular nerves

details.label: Roots
details.value: C3–C4

pearl: Share C3–C4 roots with the phrenic nerve (C3–C5), so diaphragmatic irritation (splenic rupture, ruptured ectopic, pneumoperitoneum, subphrenic abscess) refers pain to the shoulder tip (Kehr sign).

name: Ansa cervicalis (C1–C3)
function: Loop of C1–C3 fibers on the anterior surface of the carotid sheath/IJV that supplies the infrahyoid strap muscles, which depress the hyoid and larynx during swallowing and speech.

details.label: Type
details.value: Motor

details.label: Superior root
details.value: Descendens hypoglossi: C1 fibers that travel with CN XII and leave it (where XII hooks around the occipital artery) to descend on the carotid sheath

details.label: Inferior root
details.value: Descendens cervicalis: C2–C3 fibers that descend lateral (sometimes medial) to the IJV and join the superior root at about the level of the omohyoid intermediate tendon

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Omohyoid (both bellies), sternohyoid, sternothyroid (thyrohyoid and geniohyoid get C1 directly via CN XII)

details.label: Route
details.value: Loop lies anterior to carotid sheath at about the level of the cricoid/omohyoid tendon

pearl: Sits on the carotid sheath at the carotid endarterectomy site and can be divided with little deficit; used as a donor nerve for laryngeal reinnervation after recurrent laryngeal nerve injury.

name: C1 fibers traveling with CN XII (nerves to thyrohyoid and geniohyoid)
function: Ventral ramus C1 fibers hitchhike on the hypoglossal nerve below the skull base, then leave it as the superior root of the ansa and as direct branches to thyrohyoid and geniohyoid.

details.label: Type
details.value: Motor (spinal C1, not true hypoglossal fibers)

details.label: Route
details.value: Joins CN XII near the skull base, runs with it over the carotid vessels, branches off near the greater horn of the hyoid

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Thyrohyoid, geniohyoid; also gives superior root of ansa cervicalis

details.label: Root
details.value: C1 (with contribution from C2 in some)

pearl: A nuclear/medullary CN XII lesion spares thyrohyoid and geniohyoid because C1 fibers join the nerve only extracranially; a peripheral neck lesion of CN XII (e.g., carotid surgery) affects both.

name: Phrenic nerve (C3–C5)
function: Sole motor nerve to the diaphragm plus sensory supply to the central diaphragm, pericardium, and mediastinal pleura: C3, 4, 5 keeps the diaphragm alive.

details.label: Type
details.value: Mixed (motor to diaphragm, sensory to pericardium/pleura/peritoneum)

details.label: Route
details.value: Forms at lateral border of anterior scalene, descends obliquely on its anterior surface deep to prevertebral fascia, enters thorax between subclavian vein and artery

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Diaphragm (motor); central tendon, pericardium, mediastinal and diaphragmatic pleura and peritoneum (sensory)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Crossed anteriorly by transverse cervical and suprascapular arteries; thoracic duct on the left; deep to IJV and SCM

details.label: Roots
details.value: C3–C5 (C4 main)

pearl: Elevated hemidiaphragm on CXR after neck surgery, interscalene block, or mediastinal/Pancoast tumor; sniff test shows paradoxical upward motion. Irritation refers pain to the shoulder (C3–C5).

name: Nerve point of the neck (Erb's point)
function: Point at the midpoint of the posterior border of SCM where the four cutaneous branches of the cervical plexus emerge; landmark for superficial cervical plexus block.

details.label: Location
details.value: Midpoint of posterior border of SCM, about the level of the upper thyroid cartilage (C3–C4)

details.label: Nerves emerging
details.value: Lesser occipital, great auricular, transverse cervical, supraclavicular

details.label: Nearby hazards
details.value: Spinal accessory nerve exits SCM about 1 cm above; EJV crosses SCM anteriorly

details.label: Clinical use
details.value: Superficial cervical plexus block (carotid surgery, clavicle fixation, neck procedures)

pearl: Distinct from Erb's point of the brachial plexus (C5–C6 upper trunk). The spinal accessory nerve emerges just above it, so posterior-triangle lymph node biopsy here risks trapezius palsy.

name: Greater occipital nerve (C2)
function: Medial branch of the C2 dorsal ramus and largest cutaneous dorsal ramus; pierces semispinalis capitis and trapezius to supply the posterior scalp up to the vertex.

details.label: Type
details.value: Sensory (plus motor twigs to semispinalis capitis)

details.label: Route
details.value: Emerges below obliquus capitis inferior, ascends, pierces semispinalis capitis and trapezius aponeurosis about 2 cm lateral to the inion, alongside the occipital artery

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Skin of posterior scalp from the superior nuchal line to the vertex

details.label: Root
details.value: C2 dorsal ramus (medial branch)

pearl: Occipital neuralgia: paroxysmal shooting occipital pain with tenderness at its emergence; GON block 2 cm lateral to the inion (medial to the occipital artery) is diagnostic and used for migraine.

name: Third occipital nerve (C3)
function: Medial branch of the C3 dorsal ramus; supplies the C2–C3 facet joint and skin of the lower occiput and upper nuchal region, medial to the greater occipital nerve.

details.label: Type
details.value: Sensory (articular and cutaneous)

details.label: Route
details.value: Winds around the C2–C3 zygapophyseal joint, pierces semispinalis, splenius, and trapezius near the midline

details.label: Supplies
details.value: C2–C3 facet joint; skin of suboccipital and upper nuchal region

details.label: Root
details.value: C3 dorsal ramus (superficial medial branch)

pearl: Third occipital headache: cervicogenic headache from C2–C3 facet arthropathy, classically after whiplash; confirmed by third occipital nerve block and treated with radiofrequency ablation.

name: Suboccipital nerve (C1)
function: Dorsal ramus of C1; a purely motor nerve emerging in the suboccipital triangle to supply the four suboccipital muscles and, often, semispinalis capitis.

details.label: Type
details.value: Motor (usually no cutaneous branch)

details.label: Route
details.value: Emerges between the occiput and posterior arch of the atlas, below the vertebral artery, within the suboccipital triangle

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Rectus capitis posterior major and minor, obliquus capitis superior and inferior, semispinalis capitis

details.label: Relations
details.value: Vertebral artery (V3 segment) runs just above it in the groove on the atlas

pearl: Typically purely motor, no cutaneous branch (C6–C8 dorsal rami usually lack one too). Its triangle carries the vertebral artery (V3): dissection = neck pain + posterior-circulation stroke (vertigo, ataxia, diplopia).

name: Brachial plexus roots and trunks (C5–T1)
function: Ventral rami C5–T1 emerge between the anterior and middle scalenes with the subclavian artery, form upper, middle, and lower trunks in the posterior triangle, then pass under the clavicle to the axilla.

details.label: Type
details.value: Mixed

details.label: Route
details.value: Interscalene groove → supraclavicular posterior triangle → behind the clavicle over the 1st rib into the axilla

details.label: Trunks
details.value: Upper (C5–C6), middle (C7), lower (C8–T1); each divides into anterior and posterior divisions behind the clavicle

details.label: Relations
details.value: Subclavian artery with plexus between scalenes; subclavian vein anterior to anterior scalene; phrenic on anterior scalene

details.label: Roots
details.value: C5, C6, C7, C8, T1 (prefixed C4 / postfixed T2 variants)

pearl: Erb palsy (C5–C6 upper trunk): waiter's tip after birth or shoulder traction. Klumpke (C8–T1 lower trunk): claw hand ± Horner from upward arm traction or Pancoast tumor. Interscalene block spares C8–T1.

name: Dorsal scapular nerve (C5)
function: Arises from the C5 root, pierces the middle scalene, and descends deep to levator scapulae to supply the rhomboids and levator scapulae (scapular retraction and elevation).

details.label: Type
details.value: Motor

details.label: Route
details.value: C5 root → pierces middle scalene → runs with dorsal scapular artery deep to levator scapulae along the medial scapular border

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Rhomboid major, rhomboid minor, levator scapulae (with C3–C4 twigs)

details.label: Root
details.value: C5 (branch of the root, not the trunk)

pearl: Rhomboid weakness lets the scapula drift laterally with subtle winging; contrast with long thoracic palsy (medial winging on wall push) and trapezius palsy (lateral winging with shoulder droop).

name: Long thoracic nerve (C5–C7)
function: Formed from C5–C7 roots on the middle scalene; descends behind the plexus and over the 1st rib to serratus anterior, which protracts and upwardly rotates the scapula.

details.label: Type
details.value: Motor

details.label: Route
details.value: C5 and C6 roots pierce middle scalene, joined by C7; descends posterior to the plexus and clavicle onto the lateral chest wall over serratus anterior

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Serratus anterior

details.label: Roots
details.value: C5–C7 (wings of heaven)

pearl: Injured in axillary node dissection/mastectomy, stab wounds, or heavy backpack straps: medial scapular winging when pushing against a wall and inability to abduct the arm above 90 degrees.

name: Suprascapular nerve (C5–C6)
function: First branch of the upper trunk at Erb's point; runs posterolaterally across the posterior triangle to the suprascapular notch, supplying supraspinatus, infraspinatus, and the shoulder joint.

details.label: Type
details.value: Mixed (motor + articular sensory)

details.label: Route
details.value: Upper trunk → posterior triangle deep to omohyoid and trapezius → beneath the superior transverse scapular ligament through the suprascapular notch (artery passes over)

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Supraspinatus, infraspinatus; glenohumeral and acromioclavicular joints

details.label: Roots
details.value: C5–C6

pearl: Entrapment at the suprascapular notch (ganglion cyst, overhead athletes) gives shoulder pain with supraspinatus and infraspinatus atrophy; a spinoglenoid notch lesion spares supraspinatus. Army over, Navy under.

name: Cervical sympathetic trunk
function: Chain of preganglionic fibers from T1–T4 ascending behind the carotid sheath on longus colli; carries all sympathetic outflow to the head and neck through three cervical ganglia.

details.label: Type
details.value: Sympathetic (preganglionic ascending fibers; postganglionic branches)

details.label: Route
details.value: From stellate ganglion up to the skull base, posterior to the carotid sheath, anterior to prevertebral fascia, longus colli, and transverse processes

details.label: Ganglia
details.value: Superior cervical (C2–C3), middle cervical (C6), cervicothoracic/stellate (C7–T1)

details.label: Branches
details.value: Gray rami communicantes to C1–C8, superior/middle/inferior cardiac nerves, carotid and vertebral plexuses

details.label: Key fact
details.value: No white rami in the neck: preganglionic fibers enter from T1–T4 and ascend

pearl: Horner syndrome (ptosis, miosis, anhidrosis) from lesions anywhere along the pathway: Pancoast tumor, carotid dissection, neck surgery/trauma, lateral medullary stroke. Cocaine/apraclonidine drops confirm it.

name: Superior cervical ganglion
function: Largest cervical sympathetic ganglion (fused C1–C4 ganglia) at the C2–C3 level behind the ICA; its postganglionic fibers reach the eye, face, and salivary glands via the carotid plexuses.

details.label: Type
details.value: Sympathetic postganglionic cell bodies (third-order neuron of the oculosympathetic pathway)

details.label: Location
details.value: Anterior to longus capitis, posterior to the ICA and carotid sheath, at C2–C3 near the angle of the mandible

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Dilator pupillae, superior tarsal (Müller) muscle, facial sweat glands and vessels, salivary glands, pineal gland

details.label: Branches
details.value: Internal and external carotid nerves, gray rami to C1–C4, pharyngeal branches, superior cardiac nerve

pearl: Third-order (postganglionic) Horner from lesions distal to the SCG (ICA dissection, cavernous sinus) spares most facial sweating because sudomotor fibers travel with the ECA; hydroxyamphetamine fails to dilate the pupil.

name: Middle cervical ganglion
function: Small, inconstant ganglion at the C6 level near the inferior thyroid artery and cricoid; gives gray rami to C5–C6 and the middle cardiac nerve, and may fuse with the stellate ganglion.

details.label: Type
details.value: Sympathetic postganglionic cell bodies

details.label: Location
details.value: Anterior to the inferior thyroid artery at the level of the cricoid cartilage/C6 (Chassaignac's carotid tubercle)

details.label: Branches
details.value: Gray rami to C5–C6, middle cardiac nerve, branches to the thyroid gland and inferior thyroid artery

details.label: Connections
details.value: Ansa subclavia loops anterior to the subclavian artery to join the stellate ganglion

pearl: At risk during thyroidectomy near the inferior thyroid artery and in anterior approaches to the C5–C6 spine (postoperative Horner); the ansa subclavia encircles the subclavian artery.

name: Stellate (cervicothoracic) ganglion
function: Fusion of the inferior cervical and T1 ganglia anterior to the neck of the 1st rib and C7 transverse process, behind the vertebral artery origin; relay for sympathetics to the upper limb and head.

details.label: Type
details.value: Sympathetic (white ramus enters only from T1, sometimes T2; preganglionic fibers from T1–T4 ascend through it; postganglionic cell bodies)

details.label: Location
details.value: Anterior to C7 transverse process and neck of the 1st rib, posterior to the vertebral and subclavian arteries, posteromedial to anterior scalene, near the pleural cupola

details.label: Branches
details.value: Gray rami to C7, C8, T1; inferior cardiac nerve; vertebral nerve and plexus; ansa subclavia

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Upper limb vasomotor/sudomotor supply, heart, and onward fibers to the head via the trunk

pearl: Stellate block (at the C6 Chassaignac tubercle) for CRPS and refractory VT; Horner confirms success. Risks: pneumothorax, vertebral artery injection (seizure), hoarseness. Pancoast tumor compresses it → Horner.

name: Internal carotid nerve and plexus (Horner's pathway)
function: Postganglionic sympathetic fibers from the SCG ascend as the internal carotid nerve/plexus on the ICA through the carotid canal to the dilator pupillae, superior tarsal muscle, and deep petrosal nerve.

details.label: Type
details.value: Sympathetic postganglionic

details.label: Route
details.value: SCG → internal carotid nerve → plexus in the carotid canal → cavernous sinus → joins CN V1 (nasociliary/long ciliary nerves) and the ophthalmic artery into the orbit

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Dilator pupillae, superior tarsal (Müller) muscle, orbital vessels; deep petrosal nerve → vidian nerve → nasal/lacrimal vasomotor fibers

details.label: Oculosympathetic pathway
details.value: Hypothalamus → ciliospinal center C8–T2 → stellate → SCG → carotid plexus → eye

pearl: ICA dissection (neck trauma, chiropractic manipulation) causes painful Horner syndrome without facial anhidrosis plus risk of ischemic stroke, because the carotid plexus rides on the dissected vessel.

name: Gray rami communicantes (cervical)
function: Unmyelinated postganglionic fibers from the three cervical ganglia to every cervical spinal nerve; distribute vasomotor, sudomotor, and pilomotor supply to neck and upper limb dermatomes.

details.label: Type
details.value: Sympathetic postganglionic

details.label: Route
details.value: SCG → C1–C4; middle ganglion → C5–C6; stellate → C7–C8 (and T1). From the trunk (anterior to the transverse processes, on longus colli/capitis) rami pass posterolaterally to join the ventral rami in the transverse-process grooves, where the rami lie behind the vertebral artery

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Sweat glands, arrector pili, and cutaneous vessels in cervical and brachial plexus territories

details.label: Key fact
details.value: Cervical spinal nerves have gray rami only; no white rami (preganglionic fibers enter the trunk from T1–T4)

pearl: Because cervical nerves lack white rami, all head and neck sympathetic preganglionic fibers exit at T1–T4: an apical lung (Pancoast) lesion interrupts the whole outflow, giving Horner with facial anhidrosis.

name: Optic chiasm
function: Decussation of nasal retinal fibers from both optic nerves; sits above the pituitary fossa and continues as the optic tracts, so each tract carries the contralateral visual field.

details.label: Type
details.value: Sensory (special visual); CNS white-matter tract, not a true peripheral nerve

details.label: Location/route
details.value: Suprasellar, above diaphragma sellae and pituitary gland, anterior to the infundibulum; lies in the floor of the third ventricle (optic recess), just below the lamina terminalis

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Receives both optic nerves; gives rise to right and left optic tracts to the lateral geniculate nuclei

details.label: Fibers
details.value: Nasal retinal fibers (temporal fields) cross; temporal retinal fibers (nasal fields) remain ipsilateral

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior hypophyseal arteries, anterior cerebral and anterior communicating branches

pearl: Bitemporal hemianopia = chiasmal compression (pituitary adenoma, craniopharyngioma): check prolactin, visual fields, MRI sella. Pituitary apoplexy adds sudden headache and ophthalmoplegia.

name: Trigeminal (Gasserian/semilunar) ganglion
function: Sensory ganglion of CN V holding cell bodies of V1–V3 primary afferents (except proprioception); lies in Meckel's cave on the petrous apex and gives rise to the three divisions.

details.label: Type
details.value: Sensory (pseudounipolar cell bodies); motor root of V3 passes beneath it without synapsing

details.label: Location/route
details.value: Meckel's cave (dural pouch) on trigeminal impression of petrous apex, middle cranial fossa, lateral to cavernous sinus

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Face, anterior scalp, cornea, oral and nasal mucosa, teeth, supratentorial dura

details.label: Branches
details.value: V1 ophthalmic (superior orbital fissure), V2 maxillary (foramen rotundum), V3 mandibular (foramen ovale)

pearl: HSV-1 latency site (cold sores); VZV reactivation gives zoster ophthalmicus (V1, Hutchinson sign). Trigeminal neuralgia refractory to carbamazepine: microvascular decompression or ganglion rhizotomy.

name: Geniculate ganglion
function: Sensory ganglion of CN VII at the first bend (genu) of the facial canal; holds taste cell bodies for the anterior tongue and is where the greater petrosal nerve leaves the facial nerve.

details.label: Type
details.value: Sensory (taste, external ear skin); motor and parasympathetic fibers pass through without synapsing

details.label: Location/route
details.value: First genu of the facial canal in the petrous temporal bone, medial wall of the middle ear near the cochlea

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Taste from anterior 2/3 tongue (via chorda tympani) and soft palate; skin of concha and ear canal

details.label: Branches
details.value: Greater petrosal nerve (lacrimation, nasal/palatal glands); nerve continues to stapedius branch and chorda tympani

pearl: VZV reactivation here = Ramsay Hunt syndrome: ipsilateral facial palsy + vesicles in ear canal/auricle, often with hearing loss/vertigo; treat with valacyclovir + prednisone. Lesion here also drops lacrimation.

name: Supratrochlear nerve
function: Smaller medial terminal branch of the frontal nerve (V1); exits the orbit above the trochlea to supply skin of the medial forehead, medial upper eyelid, and adjacent conjunctiva.

details.label: Type
details.value: Sensory (general somatic afferent), branch of V1 via frontal nerve

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Leaves orbit at the superomedial angle above the trochlea of superior oblique, pierces frontalis, ascends medial forehead

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Medial forehead and anterior midline scalp, medial upper eyelid, conjunctiva; medial to supraorbital territory

details.label: Branches
details.value: Palpebral twigs and ascending frontal/scalp twigs; communicates with infratrochlear nerve

pearl: Forehead/anterior scalp laceration block: infiltrate supraorbital + supratrochlear nerves along the superior orbital rim medial to the pupil. Both are V1, so spared in V2/V3 zoster.

name: Short and long ciliary nerves
function: Short ciliary nerves carry postganglionic parasympathetics (ciliary ganglion) to sphincter pupillae and ciliary muscle; long ciliary nerves carry sympathetics to dilator pupillae plus corneal sensation.

details.label: Type
details.value: Mixed autonomic + sensory: short = parasympathetic (+ passing sympathetic and sensory); long = sympathetic + sensory

details.label: Route
details.value: Short (6–10) leave ciliary ganglion; long (2–3) branch from nasociliary nerve; all pierce sclera around the optic nerve

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Short: sphincter pupillae (miosis), ciliary muscle (accommodation). Long: dilator pupillae (mydriasis), cornea, iris, ciliary body

details.label: Fibers
details.value: Parasympathetics: Edinger-Westphal → CN III → ciliary ganglion. Sympathetics: superior cervical ganglion → carotid plexus → nasociliary

pearl: Pupil-involving CN III palsy = compression (PCom aneurysm, uncal herniation) as parasympathetics run superficially; Adie tonic pupil = ciliary ganglion lesion, hypersensitive to dilute pilocarpine.

name: Motor branches of V3 (masseteric, deep temporal, pterygoid, tensor nerves)
function: Branchial motor fibers of CN V3 leaving via foramen ovale to the muscles of mastication (masseter, temporalis, medial/lateral pterygoid) plus tensor veli palatini and tensor tympani.

details.label: Type
details.value: Motor (special visceral efferent, first pharyngeal arch); motor root bypasses the trigeminal ganglion

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Foramen ovale → infratemporal fossa; masseteric nerve crosses the mandibular notch, deep temporal nerves ascend beneath temporalis

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Masseter, temporalis, medial and lateral pterygoid, tensor veli palatini, tensor tympani (mylohyoid/anterior digastric via nerve to mylohyoid)

details.label: Branches
details.value: Masseteric, anterior and posterior deep temporal, lateral pterygoid, medial pterygoid (gives tensor nerves via otic ganglion, no synapse)

pearl: V3 motor lesion: jaw deviates TOWARD the lesion on opening (unopposed contralateral lateral pterygoid) with masseter/temporalis wasting. Hyperacusis points to stapedius (CN VII), not tensor tympani.

name: Deep petrosal nerve / nerve of the pterygoid canal (Vidian nerve)
function: Deep petrosal nerve brings postganglionic sympathetics from the internal carotid plexus; it joins the greater petrosal nerve at foramen lacerum to form the Vidian nerve, which runs to the pterygopalatine ganglion.

details.label: Type
details.value: Autonomic: postganglionic sympathetic (deep petrosal) + preganglionic parasympathetic (greater petrosal), plus some palatal taste

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Internal carotid plexus → deep petrosal nerve → unites with greater petrosal at foramen lacerum → pterygoid (Vidian) canal → pterygopalatine fossa

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Lacrimal gland; mucous glands and vessels of nasal cavity, palate, nasopharynx (distributed on V2 branches and zygomatic–lacrimal communication)

details.label: Branches
details.value: Terminates in the pterygopalatine ganglion; sympathetic fibers pass through without synapsing

pearl: Vidian canal is the endoscopic landmark for the petrous internal carotid in skull base surgery; Vidian neurectomy once treated refractory vasomotor rhinitis. Dry eye + dry nose localizes proximal to the PPG.

name: Cervical spinal nerve roots (C1–C8)
function: Eight paired mixed spinal nerves formed from dorsal and ventral roots; each exits its intervertebral foramen ABOVE the same-numbered vertebra (C8 below C7) to form the cervical and brachial plexuses.

details.label: Type
details.value: Mixed: motor ventral root + sensory dorsal root (dorsal root ganglion sits within the foramen)

details.label: Exit/route
details.value: Intervertebral foramina, bordered anteriorly by the uncovertebral joint/disc and posteriorly by the facet joint; C1 above the atlas, C8 between C7 and T1

details.label: Supplies
details.value: C1–C4 → cervical plexus (neck skin/strap muscles, diaphragm via C3–C5); C5–C8 (+T1) → brachial plexus

details.label: Key levels
details.value: C5 deltoid/biceps reflex; C6 wrist extension, brachioradialis reflex, thumb; C7 triceps reflex, middle finger; C8 finger flexors, little finger

pearl: Cervical radiculopathy: C6–C7 disc herniation compresses the C7 root (triceps weakness, lost triceps reflex, middle finger numbness); Spurling test positive. Most resolve conservatively; MRI if progressive deficit or myelopathy.
